The second issue: according to Malik and al-Shafi'i, it is not valid to feed fewer than sixty needy people. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: if he feeds one needy person each day half a sa' until he completes the number, it suffices for him.

The third issue: Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: It is a strange matter that Abu Hanifa said that the restriction of a free person is void, and he argued with His saying, exalted is He: (then the freeing of a neck), and did not distinguish between the mature and the wastrel. This is weak jurisprudence unbefitting his rank, for this verse is general, and the judgment of restraint was widespread among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and reason requires it. Whoever is under restraint due to minority or guardianship, and then becomes a wastrel, has been forbidden to hand over property to him, so how could his action be enforced concerning it when the specific governs the general?

The fourth issue: according to some scholars, the ruling on zihar abrogates the practice they had of considering zihar to be a divorce, and this meaning has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Qilaba and others.

The fifth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger﴾, meaning: that which We have described of severity in the expiation. (So that you may believe) means: so that you may affirm that God commanded it. Some scholars have used this to argue that this expiation is faith in God, exalted and glorified is He, because He mentioned it and made it obligatory, and said: (That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger), meaning: that is so that you may be obedient to God, exalted is He, standing at His limits and not transgressing them. So He named the expiation faith because it is obedience and observance of the limit. Thus it is established that everything resembling it is faith. If it is said: the meaning of His saying, "That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger," is: so that you do not return to zihar, which is an objectionable word and falsehood.
It is said to him: it may be that this is intended and the first is intended too, so the meaning is: that is so that you do not return to the objectionable word and falsehood, but rather you abandon both as obedience to God, exalted is He, since He has forbidden them; and so that you avoid the one who makes zihar with her until you make expiation, since God forbade touching her; and so that you make expiation, since God, exalted is He, commanded the expiation and required its payment from you. Thus by all this you will be believers in God and His Messenger, for these are limits you guard and acts of obedience you perform, and obedience to God and to His Messenger (ﷺ) is faith. And success is from God.

The sixth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And these are the limits of God﴾, meaning: He made clear His disobedience and His obedience. So His disobedience is zihar, and His obedience is the expiation.
(And for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment), meaning: for whoever does not affirm the rulings of God, exalted is He, is the punishment of Hell.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 5–6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾. When He mentioned the believers who stand at His limits (hudud), He mentioned those who oppose them and act against them. Al-muhadda (opposition) is enmity and contradiction regarding the limits, and it is like His saying: ﴿That is because they opposed (shaqqu) Allah and His Messenger﴾ [[See vol. 18, p. 6]]. It has also been said: (yuhadduna Allah) means the friends of Allah, as in the report: "Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine, has declared war on Me" (man aha'na li waliyyan faqad baraza-ni bil-muharabah). Al-Zajjaj said: al-muhadda is that one be on a limit that opposes the limit of one's companion. Its root meaning is restraint (al-mumana'ah), and from it comes al-hadid (iron), and from it al-haddad (the gatekeeper's bolt).

(Kubitu), Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: they were destroyed. Qatadah said: they were disgraced, just as those before them were disgraced. Ibn Zayd said: they were punished. Al-Suddi said: they were cursed. Al-Farra' said: they were enraged on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq). It was also said: on the day of Badr. The intended people are the polytheists. It was also said: the hypocrites.

(As those before them were brought low). It has also been said: (kubitu) means they will be brought low (sa-yukbatun), and this is a glad tidings from Allah the Exalted to the believers of victory, and the statement was phrased in the past tense to make the event near to the one being informed. It has also been said: it is in the dialect of Madhhij [[Madhhij, like Masjid: a tribe in Yemen.]].

(And We have certainly sent down clear signs), concerning those who opposed Allah and His Messenger from among those before them, regarding what We did to them.

(And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day﴾ is in the accusative governed by (a humiliating punishment), or by a hidden verb whose estimate is: and remember, magnifying the Day.

(On the Day Allah will resurrect them all) i.e., men and women, He will raise them from their graves in one state. (Then He will inform them) i.e., tell them (of what they did) in the world. (Allah has enumerated it) against them in the records of their deeds. (And they forgot it) themselves, until He reminds them of it through their records, so that the proof against them is more complete.

(And Allah is Witness over everything) — observing, watching, nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth?﴾ Nothing is hidden from Him, neither secret nor open.

(There is no secret conversation of three but He is their fourth) The majority of readers recite (مَا يَكُونُ) with the ya', because the feminine verb is separated from its subject. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa', al-A'raj, Abu Haywa and Isa recite (مَا تَكُونُ) with the ta', to match the feminine gender of the verb. Al-najwa (secret conversation) means private discourse (al-sirar). It is a verbal noun (masdar), and a masdar may be used as a description, as in the saying: qawm najwa, meaning people who hold a secret conversation. From this is His saying: ﴿and when they hold secret conversation﴾ [see vol. 10, p. 272]. His saying: ﴿thalathah﴾ (three) is in the genitive case because (najwa) is put in construct with it. Al-Farra' said: (thalathah) is an adjective of (najwa), so it takes the genitive, and if you wish you may make (najwa) construct with it. It would also be permissible to put it in the accusative by supposing a verb, and this is the reading of Ibn Abi Abla: (thalathatan) and (khamsatan) in the accusative, as a circumstantial accusative (hal) with an implied verb "yatanajawna" (they confer secretly), since najwa indicates it; so said al-Zamakhshari. It is also permissible to put (thalathah) in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for the position of (najwa). Then it has been said: every private conversation is a najwa. It has also been said: the najwa is what occurs in the seclusion of three who keep something secret and confer about it, while sirar is what is between two.

(He is their fourth) He knows and hears their secret conversation. This is indicated by the verse opening with knowledge and then concluding with knowledge. It has also been said: najwa derives from najwa, which is a raised part of the earth; so the two who confer withdraw and seclude their secret, like a raised part of the ground that is separated from what adjoins it. The meaning is that God's hearing encompasses every speech, and Allah indeed heard the dispute of the woman who was divorced by her husband through zihar.

(Nor less than that, nor more) Salam, Ya'qub, Abu al-'Aliyah, Nasr and Isa recite (lā adnā) and (lā akthar) in the nominative, on the position of (min najwa) before (min) entered, since its underlying sense is "what is a najwa". (Thalathah) may also be nominative, on the position of (illa) together with (adnā), as in your saying: "There is no power or strength except by Allah," with the first "power" pronounced with a fatha and the second with a damma. It is also permissible that both be nominative as initial subjects, as in your saying: "There is no power or strength except by Allah." The explanation of this has been fully given in (al-Baqarah) [see vol. 3, p. 266 onward]. Al-Zuhri and Ikrimah recite (akbar) with the ba' (b). The common reading has the tha' and a fatha on the ra', following the wording, while its position is genitive. Al-Farra' said regarding His saying: (There is no secret conversation of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth): he said: the meaning is that the number is not intended, since He, may He be exalted, intended only that He, being fully aware, is with every number, whether few or many, and knows what they say secretly and openly, and nothing is hidden from Him; therefore He suffices with mentioning some of the numbers and not others. It has also been said: the meaning is that Allah is with them by His knowledge wherever they are, without departing or moving. This was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who had done something in secret, and Allah informed them that this is not hidden from Him; this was said by Ibn Abbas. Qatadah and Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning the Jews.

(Then He will inform them) He will tell them (of what they did) of good and evil (on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is Knower of all things).

Al-Qurtubi's commentary on Surah 58, verse 8:

The first issue concerns His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret consultation?﴾ It has been said that this refers to the Jews and the hypocrites, as we have previously mentioned. It has also been said that it refers to the Muslims. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed concerning the Jews and the hypocrites, who used to hold secret consultations among themselves, looking at the believers and winking at one another. The believers would say: Perhaps they have received news about our brothers and relatives among the Muhajirun and the Ansar of a killing, a calamity, or a defeat, and that grieves them. So the complaints of the believers to the Prophet ﷺ increased, and he forbade them from secret consultation, but they did not desist, and so it was revealed. Muqatil said: There was a truce (muwada'ah) between the Prophet ﷺ and the Jews, and whenever a man of the believers passed by them, they would consult secretly among themselves until the believer thought something evil, and so he would turn aside from his path. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade them, but they did not desist, and so it was revealed. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: A man would come to the Prophet ﷺ, ask him for a need, and consult with him privately, while the land at that time was at war, so they would suppose that he was consulting him about war, a calamity, or a serious matter, and they would be alarmed by this, and so it was revealed.

The second issue: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that he said: One night we were conversing when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said: (What is this secret consultation? Were you not forbidden from secret consultation?) We said: We repent to Allah, O Messenger of Allah; we were mentioning the Masih, meaning the Dajjal, out of fear of him. He said: (Shall I not inform you of what I fear for you more than him?) We said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: (Hidden shirk: that a man stands up to perform an action so that another man may see it.) Al-Mawardi mentioned it.

Hamzah, Khalaf and Ruways on the authority of Ya'qub recited (wa-yantajuna) in the form of yaftaʿiluna, and this is the recitation of ʿAbd Allah and his companions. The rest recited (wa-yatanajawna) in the form of yatafaʿalawna, and this was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim, due to His saying, exalted is He: (idha tanajaytum) and (tatanajaw). Al-Nahhas said: Sibawayh related that tafaʿala and iftaʿala come with the same meaning, such as takhasamu and ikhtasamu, and taqatalu and iqtatalu. Accordingly, (yatanajawna) and (yantajuna) are one and the same. The meaning of (bil-ithmi wal-ʿudwan) is falsehood and injustice.

(Wa-maʿsiyat al-Rasul) means opposing him. Al-Dahhak, Mujahid and Humayd recited (wa-maʿsiyat al-Rasul) in the plural.

The third issue concerns His saying, exalted is He: (When they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you.) There is no disagreement among the transmitters that the intended ones are the Jews. They would come to the Prophet ﷺ and say: As-sam ʿalayka (death be upon you). They intended by this the greeting outwardly, while inwardly they meant death. The Prophet ﷺ would say: (ʿAlaykum), in one narration, and in another narration (wa-ʿalaykum). Ibn al-ʿArabi said: It is problematic. They used to say: If Muhammad were a prophet, Allah would not have let us go unpunished for reviling him and mocking him. They were ignorant that the Creator, exalted is He, is forbearing and does not hasten to punish one who reviles Him, so how much less one who reviles His Prophet. It is established that the Prophet ﷺ said: (No one is more patient with harm than Allah; they ascribe to Him a consort and a son, yet He pardons them and provides for them.) So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this as an uncovering of their inner secrets, an exposure of their hidden intentions, and a miracle for His Messenger ﷺ. It is established from Qatadah, from Anas, that a Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions and said: As-sam ʿalaykum. The Prophet ﷺ returned the greeting and said: (Do you know what this one said?) They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: (He said such-and-such; bring him back to me.) They brought him back, and he said: (Did you say, "As-sam ʿalaykum"?) He said: Yes. Then the Prophet ﷺ said at that time: (When the People of the Book greet you, say: "ʿAlayka ma qulta" [upon you what you said].) So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: (When they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you.)

I say: al-Tirmidhi recorded it and said: This is a hasan sahih hadith. It is also established from ʿAisha that she said: Some Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: As-sam ʿalayka, O Abu al-Qasim. I said: As-sam ʿalaykum, and may Allah do to you and do to you. The Prophet, upon him peace, said: (Mahh, O ʿAisha, for Allah does not love obscenity or the use of obscenity.) I said: O Messenger of Allah, do you not see what they say? He said: (Do you not see that I return to them what they say? I say: "wa-ʿalaykum.") So this verse was revealed: (with that by which Allah has not greeted you), meaning: Allah has greeted you with peace, while they say "as-sam ʿalayka," and as-sam means death. Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded it in meaning. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: (When the People of the Book greet you, say: "wa-ʿalaykum.") Thus the narration is (wa-ʿalaykum) with the waw, which the scholars have discussed, because the conjunctive waw requires association, so it would follow that one enters with them into what they invoked against us, namely death, or the weariness of our religion, which is boredom. It is said: sa'imа yas'amu sa'amatan wa-sa'aman. Some said: the waw is superfluous, as it is superfluous in the saying of the poet:

"So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he turned aside,"

meaning: when we passed, he turned aside, so the waw was added. Others said: it is for resumption, as if he said: "And as-sam ʿalaykum." Others said: it remains in its original function of conjunction, and that does not harm us, because we are answered against them but they are not answered against us, as the Prophet ﷺ said. Al-Zubayr narrated that he heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: Some Jews greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: As-sam ʿalayka, O Abu al-Qasim. He said: (Wa-ʿalaykum). ʿAisha said, angered: Did you not hear what they said? He said: (Yes, I have heard, and I returned it to them, and we are answered against them but they are not answered against us.) Muslim recorded it. The narration with the waw is better in meaning, and its affirmation is more authentic in transmission and more widely known. There has been disagreement concerning returning the greeting to the people of the covenant (ahl al-dhimmah): is it obligatory as returning the greeting to Muslims is? Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi and Qatadah held this view, based on the command to do so. Malik, according to what Ashhab and Ibn Wahb related from him, held that it is not obligatory; so if you return it, say: ʿAlayka. Ibn Tawus preferred that one say in returning to them: ʿAlakas-salam, meaning, may it be raised from you. Some of our companions preferred: al-Silam with a kasrah on the sin, meaning stones. What Malik said is more preferable, following the Sunnah, and Allah knows best. Masruq narrated from ʿAisha, who said: Some Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: As-sam ʿalayka, O Abu al-Qasim. He said: (Wa-ʿalaykum). ʿAisha said: I said: Rather, upon you is as-sam and adh-dhamm. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O ʿAisha, do not be obscene.) She said: Did you not hear what they said? He said: (Did I not return to them what they said? I said: wa-ʿalaykum.) In another narration: ʿAisha perceived them and reviled them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Mahh, O ʿAisha, for Allah does not love obscenity or the use of obscenity.) He added: Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: (When they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you), to the end of the verse. Adh-dham, with the mim lightened, means blame. In the proverb: "The beautiful woman never lacks blame (dhamm)," meaning a fault. It may be pronounced with hamza or without hamza: it is said dhaʾamahu yadhʾamuhu, like dhaʾaba yadhʾabu, and the passive participle is madhʾum, with hamza, and from it (madhmuman madhhuran). It is also said dhamahu yadhumuhu, with lightening, like ramahu yarumuhu.

His saying, exalted is He: (And they say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?") They said: If Muhammad were a prophet, Allah would punish us for what we say, so why does Allah not punish us? It has been said: They said that he responds to us and says, "And upon you is as-sam," and as-sam is death; so if he were a prophet, he would be answered concerning us and we would die. This is a matter of wonder on their part, for they were People of the Book, and they knew that prophets may be angered, yet the one who angers them is not hastened with punishment.

(Hasbuhum Jahannam) means: Jahannam is sufficient for them as punishment tomorrow (ghadan). (Fa-bi'sa al-masir) means: the destination, the place of return.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you confer privately﴾ He forbade the believers from conferring privately among themselves, as the hypocrites and the Jews did. So He said: (O you who have believed, when you confer privately), meaning: when you speak secretly with one another (tasarartum).

(So do not confer privately) — this is the reading of the common readers (qira'at al-'ammah). Yahya ibn Wthdhab (Yahya ibn Wathhab), 'Asim, and Ruways from Ya'qub read (fa-la tantajau) from al-intija' (the act of confiding in secret): ﴿with sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾, ﴿but confer with one another in righteousness﴾, meaning in obedience, ﴿and piety﴾, meaning by abstaining from what Allah has forbidden. It is also said that the address is to the hypocrites, meaning: O you who have believed according to their claim. It is also said: meaning, O you who have believed in Musa (Moses).

﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, meaning: you will be assembled in the Hereafter.

There are two issues here.

The first concerns His saying, ﴿Secret counsel is only from Satan﴾, meaning it comes from Satan's embellishment, "so that it may grieve those who believe" (ليحزن الذين آمنوا), when they imagine that the Muslims have suffered setbacks in the *sarāyā* (small military expeditions), or when they see them gathering to plot against the Muslims. Sometimes they would confer privately with the Prophet ﷺ, and the Muslims would think that they were belittling them in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ. "And it does not harm them at all" (وليس بضارهم شيئا إلا بإذن الله), that is, the private conversation, "except by the permission of Allah," that is, by His will. It was also said: by His knowledge. And it is related from Ibn Abbas: by His command.

"And upon Allah let the believers rely" (وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون), that is, they entrust their affairs to Him, they commit all their matters to His help, and they seek refuge in Him from Satan and from every evil. It is He who empowered Satan with whisperings as a trial and a test for the servant. Had He willed, He would have turned it away from him.

The second issue: In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When there are three, two should not confer privately to the exclusion of the third." And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you are three, two should not confer privately to the exclusion of the other until you mix with the people, because that would grieve him." In this hadith he clarified the ultimate purpose of the prohibition, which is that the third person should find someone to converse with, as Ibn Umar did. That is, he was speaking with a man when another came wishing to confer with him, but he did not confer with him until he called a fourth, and then he said to him and to the first man: "Step back." Then he conferred with the man who had sought the private conversation. It was transmitted by Malik in al-Muwatta'. In it there is also an indication of the reason given in the words: "because that would grieve him," that is, something arises in his heart that grieves him on account of it. This happens when he imagines that they are speaking about him in a way he dislikes, or that they do not regard him as worthy of being included in their conversation, and other such suggestions of Satan and whisperings of the self. All of this arises from his being alone; when someone else is with him, he is safe from it. On this basis, all numbers are equal in this regard: four should not confer privately to the exclusion of one, nor ten, nor a thousand, for example, since that same reason exists in their case. Indeed, its occurrence in a large group is more likely and more probable, so prohibiting it there is all the more fitting. The reason the hadith mentions three specifically is that it is the first number in which this meaning can arise. The apparent meaning of the hadith covers all times and all circumstances, and this is the view of Ibn Umar, Malik and the majority. Whether the private conversation concerns something recommended, permissible or obligatory, grief still results from it. Some people have held that this ruling applied at the beginning of Islam, because at that time it was the situation of the hypocrites, who would confer privately to the exclusion of the believers; but when Islam spread, this ruling lapsed. Others said: this applies specifically to travel, in places where a man cannot feel safe with his companion. But in a settled area, among inhabited places, it does not apply, because there one finds someone to help him. Travel, by contrast, is a place where assassination is likely and where there is no one to give aid. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 11:

There are seven issues concerning it.

The first issue is His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you are told to make room in the assemblies﴾ [The source reading of Nafi' has "in the assembly" in the singular]. When He made clear that the Jews greeted the Prophet with a greeting with which Allah had not greeted him, and censured them for it, He linked to it the command to refine manners in sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they would not crowd him in the assembly. He also commanded the Muslims to be kind and affectionate, so that some would make room for others, and so that they could hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and look at him. Qatadah and Mujahid said: They used to compete for places in the assembly of the Prophet (ﷺ), so they were commanded that some should make room for others. Al-Dahhak said the same. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by this are the gatherings of battle, when they lined up for war. Al-Hasan and Yazid ibn Abi Habib said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the polytheists, his Companions would vie for the first row, so they would not make room for one another, out of eagerness for fighting and martyrdom, and so this was revealed. This is like His saying: ﴿stations for fighting﴾ [see vol. 4, p. 184]. Muqatil said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was in the Suffah (a raised area attached to the Prophet's mosque where poor Companions lived), and on Friday the place was cramped. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to honour the people of Badr from the Emigrants and the Helpers. Some people of Badr came, among them Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and they had been preceded to the assembly. They stood opposite the Prophet (ﷺ) on their feet, waiting for room to be made for them, but they were not given room. This grieved the Prophet (ﷺ), so he said to those around him from [others than] the people of Badr: "Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so," matching the number of those standing from the people of Badr. This was hard on those who were made to stand, and the Prophet (ﷺ) perceived the dislike in their faces. The hypocrites made insinuations and said: "These people have not been fair, though they loved closeness to their Prophet, yet they preceded others to the place." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

(﴿Make room﴾) means: make space. "Fulan made room for his brother in his assembly" (fasaha yafsahu fashan), that is, he was made room for. From this come the expressions "a spacious land" (balad fasih) and "you have leeway in such-and-such" (laka fi kadha fusha). Fasaha yafsahu, like mana'a yamna'u, means he widened the assembly. Fasuha yafsuhu fasaha, like karuma yakrumu karamatan, means he became spacious; from this comes "a spacious place" (makan fasih).

The second issue: Al-Sulami, Zirr ibn Hubaysh and Asim read (fi al-majalis) in the plural. Qatadah, Dawud ibn Abi Hind and al-Hasan, with variant reports from him, read (idha qila lakum tafasahu) [with the verb in the form tafa'alu]. The rest read (tafassahu fi al-majlis) in the singular. Whoever reads the plural: His saying (tafassahu fi al-majalis) indicates that each person has a place of sitting. The same applies if war is meant. The same is also permissible if the mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) is meant, and the plural is used because each sitter has a seat. It is also permissible, if the singular (al-majlis) is meant, to mean the assembly of the Prophet (ﷺ). It may also be that the singular is meant as a generic noun, as in their saying: "The dinar and the dirham have become plentiful." I say: The correct view regarding the verse is that it is general to every gathering in which Muslims assemble for good and reward, whether it is a gathering of war, of remembrance, or the Friday gathering. Each person has more right to the place he got to first. [The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever precedes to what no one has preceded to has more right to it."] [This addition is from the margin of al-Jamal, quoting al-Qurtubi.] However, one should make room for his brother as long as he is not harmed, and as long as the crowding does not push him out of his place. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "A man should not make a man get up from his place and then sit in it." And from him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he forbade a man to be made to get up from his place so that another could sit in it, but rather: "Make room and widen." Ibn Umar used to dislike that a man should get up from his place and then be seated in his place. This is the wording of al-Bukhari.

The third issue: If one of the people sits in a place in the mosque, it is not permissible for another to make him get up until the other sits in his place. This is because Muslim narrated from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Let none of you make his brother get up on Friday and then go to his seat and sit in it. Rather, let him say: Make room." 

Branch: If the seated person gets up until someone else takes his place, it is examined. If the place he moved to is equal to the first in hearing the words of the imam, then it is not disliked for him. If it is further from the imam, then it is disliked for him, because in that case he loses his share.

The fourth issue: If a person tells another to go early to the congregational mosque and take a place for him to sit in, this is not disliked. When the one who gave the order arrives, the other should get up from the place. This is based on what is reported: that Ibn Sirin used to send his servant to a seat of his on Friday, and he would sit there for him; when Ibn Sirin came, he got up from it for him.

Branch: On this basis, whoever sends a rug or a prayer mat to be spread for him in a place in the mosque [the manuscripts Z, S, H and L have a blank space here after the words "in the mosque," and the copyist noted in the margin: "a blank in the original"].

The fifth issue: Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If one of you gets up [and in the hadith of Abu Awanah: whoever gets up from his seat] and then returns to it, he has more right to it." Our scholars said: This indicates the soundness of the view that the sitter has an obligation to be given priority in his place until he gets up from it, because if he has more right to it after getting up, then before getting up he has even more right and greater claim to it. It has also been said: This is recommended, because it is a place not owned by anyone, neither before sitting nor after. There is scrutiny in this view, and it is that one might say: Granted that it is not owned, yet he has priority in it until his purpose is finished, so it becomes as if he owns its benefit, since others are prevented from competing with him for it. And Allah knows best.

The sixth issue: His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Allah will make room for you﴾, that is, in your graves. It has also been said: in your hearts. It has also been said: He will widen things for you in this world and the Hereafter.

(﴿And when you are told to rise, then rise﴾). Nafi', Ibn Amir and Asim read both occurrences with a damma on the shin [inshuzu and fansuzu]. The rest read with a kasra. Both are dialectal forms, like (ya'kufun) and (ya'rishun) [see vol. 7, pp. 272–273]. The meaning is: stand up to prayer, to jihad, and to doing good, so said most of the exegetes. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: when you are called to prayer, rise to it. This was because some men were slow to go to prayer, so this was revealed. Al-Hasan and Mujahid also said: that is, rise to war. Ibn Zayd said: This refers to the house of the Prophet (ﷺ). Each of them loved that his last meeting with the Prophet (ﷺ) should be his last moment with him, so Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when you are told to rise﴾ from the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿then rise﴾, for he has needs, so do not linger. Qatadah said: The meaning is: respond when you are called to a matter of goodness. This is the correct view, because it is general. 

Al-nashz (height) means elevation, derived from nashz al-ard, which is its rising ground. One says nashaza yanshuzu and yanshizu when he withdraws from his place, that is, rises from it. A woman who is nashiz (rebellious) is one who turns away from her husband. The origin of this is from al-nashz, and al-nashz is what rises from the ground and stands apart; this was mentioned by al-Nahhas.

The seventh issue: His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾, that is, in reward in the Hereafter and in honour in this world. So He raises the believer above the non-believer, and the scholar above the non-scholar. Ibn Mas'ud said: Allah praised the scholars in this verse. The meaning is that Allah raises those who have been given knowledge [the meaning: raises those of the believers who have been given knowledge] above those who believe but have not been given knowledge, (﴿by degrees﴾), that is, degrees in their religion when they do what they were commanded. It has also been said: The wealthy people disliked that someone wearing wool would crowd them, so they raced to the assembly of the Prophet (ﷺ), and so the address is to them. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a wealthy man gathering his garment in aversion from a poor man who wanted to sit next to him, and he said: "O so-and-so, I fear that your wealth will spread to him, or his poverty to you." This verse makes clear that elevation with Allah, exalted is He, is by knowledge and faith, not by precedence in seating at assemblies. It has also been said: By those who have been given knowledge He meant those who recite the Quran. Yahya ibn Yahya said, from Malik: (﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe﴾) are the Companions, (﴿and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾): Allah raises by them the scholar and the seeker of truth.

I say: The generality is more fitting for the issue and more appropriate to the meaning of the verse. So He raises the believer by his faith first, then by his knowledge second. In the Sahih it is reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to give precedence to Abdullah ibn Abbas over the Companions. They spoke to him about that, so he called them and called Ibn Abbas, and asked them about the interpretation of (﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾) [see vol. 20, p. 229]. They were silent. Ibn Abbas said: It is the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which Allah informed him of. Umar said: I know nothing of it except what you know. In al-Bukhari, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfah ibn Badr came and stayed with his nephew al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn, who was among the group whom Umar used to bring close, and the reciters were the companions of Umar's assemblies and consultations, whether they were elderly or young. [The hadith] and it has already passed at the end of (al-A'raf) [see vol. 7, p. 357]. In Sahih Muslim, Nafi' ibn Abd al-Harith met Umar at Usfan, and Umar used to appoint him over Makkah. Umar said: Whom have you appointed over the people of the valley? He said: Ibn Abza. He said: And who is Ibn Abza? He said: A freedman from among our freedmen. He said: You have appointed a freedman over them! He said: He is a reciter of the Book of Allah, and he is knowledgeable in the laws of inheritance. Umar said: Indeed your Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah raises by this Book some peoples and lowers others by it." The beginning of this book has already passed [see vol. 1, p. 6]. The discussion of the virtue of knowledge and scholars has passed in other places in this book [see vol. 14, p. 343] [and praise be to Allah]. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Between the scholar and the worshipper there are a hundred degrees, between each two degrees is the distance a well-trained racehorse runs in seventy years." And from him (ﷺ): "The virtue of the scholar over the worshipper is like the virtue of the full moon over the rest of the stars." And from him, peace be upon him: "Three will intercede on the Day of Resurrection: the prophets, then the scholars, then the martyrs." How great is a station that lies between prophethood and martyrdom, by the testimony of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is related from Ibn Abbas: Sulayman, peace be upon him, was given the choice between knowledge, wealth and kingship, and he chose knowledge, so wealth and kingship were given to him along with it.

**First issue:** The verse says, "O you who believe, when you confer privately with the Messenger" (﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا ناجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ﴾). The word *najaytum* (ناجَيْتُمْ) means *sārartum* (سارَرْتُمْ), that is, "you spoke to him in secret."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed because the Muslims were asking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so many questions that they wearied him. Allah, may He be exalted, wished to lighten the burden on His Prophet (ﷺ). When this verse was revealed, many people refrained. Then Allah granted them ease through the verse that follows it.

Al-Hasan said: It was revealed because some Muslims would seek out the Prophet (ﷺ) alone and confer with him privately. Some other Muslims suspected them of disparaging them in their private conversations, and this grieved them. So Allah, may He be exalted, commanded them to give charity before private conferring, in order to cut them off from seeking his solitude.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed because the hypocrites and the Jews would confer privately with the Prophet (ﷺ) and say, "He is an ear that hears everything that is said to him," and he would not prevent anyone from conferring with him. This grieved the Muslims, because Satan would put into their hearts that they had conferred with him in order to plan that groups had gathered to fight him. He said: So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when you confer privately, do not confer privately in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger﴾, and the verse continues. They did not desist, so Allah revealed this verse. The people of falsehood then refrained from private conferring, because they did not offer charity before their private conversations. This was hard on the people of faith, and they refrained from private conferring because many of them lacked the means to give charity. So Allah lightened the burden on them through what follows the verse.

**Second issue:** Ibn al-ʿArabi said: This report from Zayd contains evidence that rulings are not established according to considerations of benefit (*maṣāliḥ*). Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, and then He abrogated it (*naskh*, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) even though it was better and purer.

This is a great refutation of the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة), who insist that Allah must always act for the best interest of His servants. However, the narrator of this report from Zayd is his son ʿAbd al-Rahman, whom the scholars have declared weak. The matter in His words, ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, is a text (*naṣṣ*) that is transmitted widely (*mutawātir*) as a refutation of the Muʿtazilah. And Allah knows best.

**Third issue:** Al-Tirmidhi narrated from ʿAli ibn ʿAlqamah al-Anmari, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿O you who believe, when you confer privately with the Messenger, offer charity before your private conference﴾, [I asked him] [[Addition from manuscripts ḥ, z, s, l, h.]] the Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "What do you think of a dinar?" I said: "They cannot afford it." He said: "Then half a dinar?" I said: "They cannot afford it." He said: "How much then?" I said: "A barley grain." He said: "You are indeed frugal." He said: Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private conference?﴾, and the verse continues. He said: Because of me, Allah lightened the burden on this Ummah. [[The phrase "fa-bī" (فبى) is missing from manuscript l.]]

Abu ʿIsa (al-Tirmidhi) said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we only know it through this chain. The meaning of his words, "a barley grain," is the weight of a barley grain of gold.

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: This indicates two fine principles of legal theory (*uṣūl*): The first is the abrogation of an act of worship before it is performed. The second is considering measured quantities by analogy (*qiyās*), contrary to Abu Hanifa.

I say: It appears that the abrogation occurred only after the charity was given. It is also narrated from Mujahid that the first person to give charity for this was ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, when he conferred privately with the Prophet (ﷺ). It is reported that he gave a ring in charity.

Al-Qushayri and others mentioned from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: "There is a verse in the Book of Allah that no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me, and it is: ﴿O you who believe, when you confer privately with the Messenger, offer charity before your private conference﴾. I had a dinar, so I sold it, and whenever I conferred privately with the Messenger, I gave a dirham in charity, until it was used up. Then it was abrogated by the other verse: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private conference?﴾." Likewise Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah abrogated it by the verse that follows it.

Ibn ʿUmar said: ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, had three virtues; if I had just one of them, it would be dearer to me than red camels: his marriage to Fatimah, his being given the banner on the day of Khaybar, and the verse of private conference.

﴿That is better for you﴾, that is, than holding onto it (*imsākihā*), ﴿and purer﴾ for your hearts from sins. ﴿But if you do not find [the means]﴾, meaning the poor, ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 13:

There are two issues here. The first concerns His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you apprehensive﴾. The interrogative here means confirmation (taqrir). Ibn 'Abbas said: "Are you apprehensive" means: Are you stingy with charity? It was also said: "Are you afraid?" Al-ishfaq (apprehension) is fear of something disliked; that is, you feared and were stingy with charity, and it was hard for you ﴿to offer charity before your private consultation﴾. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: That obligation lasted only ten nights and was then abrogated (nuskh). Al-Kalbi said: It lasted only one night. Ibn 'Abbas said: Only an hour of the day remained before it was abrogated. Qatadah said likewise. And Allah knows best.

The third issue concerns His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you do not do it, and Allah has forgiven you﴾. That is, Allah abrogated that ruling. This is addressed to those who had the means to give charity. ﴿So establish prayer and give zakat﴾, so the obligation of zakat abrogated this charity. This indicates the permissibility of abrogation before the act is performed. What is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, is weak, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when you do not do it﴾, and this indicates that no one had given charity at all. And Allah knows best.

﴿Obey Allah﴾ in His obligatory duties, ﴿and His Messenger﴾ in his sunnah, ﴿and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verses 14–16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who have allied themselves with a people upon whom Allah has brought His wrath?﴾ Qatadah said: They are the hypocrites (munafiqun), who allied themselves with the Jews. ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾ means: the hypocrites are neither of the Jews nor of the Muslims, but are wavering between the two, and they used to carry the news of the Muslims to the Jews. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy and Abdullah ibn Nabtal, the two hypocrites. One of them used to sit with the Prophet (ﷺ) and then pass on his conversation to the Jews. Once, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was in one of his chambers, he said: "There is about to enter upon you now a man whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eyes of a devil." Then Abdullah ibn Nabtal entered, and he was blue-eyed, dark-skinned, short, and thin-bearded. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" He swore by Allah that he had not done that. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You did." So he went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not reviled him. Then this verse was revealed. Ibn Abbas said the same meaning. Ikrimah narrated from him, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting in the shade of a tree, and the shade had nearly receded from him, when he said: "There is about to come to you now a blue-eyed man who looks at you with the look of a devil." While we were in that state, a blue-eyed man came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) called him and said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" He said: "Leave me, and I will bring them to you." He went and brought them, and they all swore that nothing of that had occurred. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all﴾ up to His saying: ﴿they are the losers﴾. The Jews are mentioned in the Qur'an, and ﴿upon whom Allah has brought His wrath﴾.

﴿Allah has prepared for them﴾, i.e., for these hypocrites, ﴿a severe punishment﴾ in Hell, and it is the lowest level (al-darak al-asfal).

﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾, i.e., evil are their deeds. ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, by which they conceal themselves from being killed. Al-Hasan and Abu al-Aliyah read ﴿إيمانهم﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah here and in (al-Munafiqun) [see vol. 18, p. 123]. That is, they made their profession of faith a shield, so their tongues professed belief out of fear of being killed, while their hearts disbelieved. ﴿So for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ in this world by being killed, and in the Hereafter by the Fire. Al-Sadd means prevention (al-man'), ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from Islam. It was also said: it refers to their being killed for disbelief because of the hypocrisy they displayed. It was also said: i.e., by spreading false rumors and discouraging the Muslims from jihad and frightening them.

Al-Qurtubi's commentary (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on Surah 58, verses 17–19:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾, meaning, from His punishment, in any way.

Muqatil said: The hypocrites said, "Muhammad claims that he will be victorious on the Day of Resurrection. Then we are truly wretched! By Allah, on the Day of Resurrection we will defend ourselves, our children and our wealth, if there is indeed a Resurrection." So it was revealed: ﴿On the Day when Allah will raise them all up﴾, meaning, for them is a humiliating punishment. On the Day He raises them up, they will swear to Him as they swear to you today. This is a strange matter: their deceiving by oaths on the Day to come, when the realities have already become self-evident. Ibn Abbas said: it is their saying, ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ (6:23). ﴿And they think that they stand on something﴾, by their denial and their oaths.

Ibn Zayd said: they thought that it would benefit them in the Hereafter.

It was also said: ﴿And they think﴾ in this world that they stand on something, because in the Hereafter they will know the truth by necessity. The first view is more apparent.

It is related from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"On the Day of Resurrection a caller will call out: 'Where are the adversaries of Allah?' Then the Qadariyya (the school that affirms human free will and denies predestination) will stand up, their faces blackened, their eyes blue, their jaws twisted, their saliva dripping. They will say, 'By Allah, we did not worship, apart from You, any sun, moon, idol or image, nor did we take any god apart from You.'" Ibn Abbas said: "They spoke the truth, by Allah! Polytheism came to them from where they did not know." Then he recited: ﴿And they think that they stand on something. Indeed, they are the liars﴾, and he said three times: "By Allah, they are the Qadariyya."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Satan has gained mastery over them﴾, meaning, he overcame and prevailed over them, that is, by his whispering in this world.

It was also said: he became strong over them. Al-Mufaddal said: he encompassed them. A fourth possibility is that it means he gathered them and joined them together. It is said, "ahwadha al-shay'," meaning he gathered it and put some of it together with the rest. When he gathers them, he has overcome them, become strong over them, and encompassed them.

﴿So he made them forget the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning, His commands regarding obedience in action. It was also said: His restraints regarding the prohibition of disobeying Him.

Forgetting (nisyan) may mean heedlessness and may mean abandonment, and both meanings are possible here. ﴿Those are the party of Satan﴾, his followers and his band. ﴿Surely, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ in their bargain, because they sold Paradise for Hellfire and sold guidance for misguidance.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 20–21:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ has preceded at the beginning of the surah. ﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾, meaning: among the total of the humiliated, not more humiliated than them. ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"﴾, meaning: Allah has decided this.

It is said: "He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet," related from Qatadah. Al-Farra' said: "Kataba" here means "qala" (said). "Inna" is for emphasis. ﴿And My messengers﴾: whoever of them is sent with war, he is victorious through war, and whoever of them is sent with proof, he is victorious through proof. Muqatil said: The believers said: "If Allah opens for us Makkah, al-Ta'if, Khaybar and what is around them, we hope that Allah will make us victorious over Persia and Byzantium." Then 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: "Do you think the Romans and the Persians are like the villages you have conquered? By Allah, they are greater in number and stronger in might than that you should think of them such things!" So the verse was revealed: ﴿I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.﴾ Its parallel is: ﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victors﴾ (see vol. 15, p. 139).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 20–21:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ has preceded at the beginning of the surah. ﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾, meaning: among the total of the humiliated, not more humiliated than them. ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"﴾, meaning: Allah has decided this.

It is said: "He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet," related from Qatadah. Al-Farra' said: "Kataba" here means "qala" (said). "Inna" is for emphasis. ﴿And My messengers﴾: whoever of them is sent with war, he is victorious through war, and whoever of them is sent with proof, he is victorious through proof. Muqatil said: The believers said: "If Allah opens for us Makkah, al-Ta'if, Khaybar and what is around them, we hope that Allah will make us victorious over Persia and Byzantium." Then 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: "Do you think the Romans and the Persians are like the villages you have conquered? By Allah, they are greater in number and stronger in might than that you should think of them such things!" So the verse was revealed: ﴿I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.﴾ Its parallel is: ﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victors﴾ (see vol. 15, p. 139).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 22:

There are two issues in this.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving (yuwaddun) those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, they love (yuhibbuna) and take as allies (yuwaliyuna) those who oppose (hadda) Allah and His Messenger. It has already been discussed [see vol. 8, p. 194]. ﴿Even if they were their fathers﴾. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning [Abd Allah ibn [Necessary addition: this was Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may Allah be pleased with him, one of the excellent and best Companions; his father Abd Allah was the chief of the hypocrites, and the verse was revealed concerning him]] Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. He sat with the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) drank some water. He said to him: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, have you left any remainder of your drink that I might give to my father, perhaps Allah will purify his heart with it?" So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave him some leftover water, and he brought it to him. Abd Allah said to him: "What is this?" He said:

"It is the leftover of the drink of the Prophet (ﷺ). I have brought it to you so that you may drink it; perhaps Allah will purify your heart with it."

His father said to him: "Why did you not bring me the urine of your mother? It is purer than this." He became angry and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Did you not permit me to kill my father?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"Rather, be gentle with him and treat him well."

Ibn Juraij said: I was told that Abu Quhafa cursed the Prophet (ﷺ), and his son Abu Bakr struck him a blow so that he fell on his face. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. He said: "Did you do that? Do not return to him." He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, if the sword had been near me, I would have killed him."

Ibn Mas'ud said: It was revealed concerning Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father Abd Allah ibn al-Jarrah on the Day of Uhud, and it was said: on the Day of Badr. Al-Jarrah used to confront Abu Ubayda and Abu Ubayda would turn away from him. When he persisted, Abu Ubayda went for him and killed him. So Allah revealed, when he killed his father: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, the verse. Al-Waqidi said: So say the people of Syria. I asked some men of the Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr, and they said: his father died before Islam. ﴿Or their sons﴾, meaning Abu Bakr, whose son Abd Allah challenged him to single combat on the Day of Badr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let us benefit by you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not know that you are to me like hearing and sight?" ﴿Or their brothers﴾, meaning Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who killed his brother Ubayd ibn Umayr on the Day of Badr. ﴿Or their clan﴾, meaning Umar ibn al-Khattab, who killed his maternal uncle al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira on the Day of Badr, and Ali and Hamza, who killed Utba, Shayba and al-Walid on the Day of Badr. It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, when he wrote to the people of Makkah about the march of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the year of the Conquest, as will be explained, if Allah wills, at the beginning of the surah "al-Mumtahana". It shows that faith is corrupted by allying with the disbelievers, even if they are relatives.

The second: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, derived from this verse the obligation of showing enmity to the Qadariyya and avoiding sitting with them.

Ashhab said, from Malik: Do not sit with the Qadariyya, and show enmity to them for the sake of Allah, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾.

I say: The meaning of the people of qadar includes all people of wrongdoing and transgression. It is narrated from al-Thawri that he said: They used to hold that it was revealed concerning those who accompany the ruler. It is narrated from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Dawud that he met al-Mansur during the circumambulation, and when he recognised him he fled from him, reciting this verse. It is also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to say:

"O Allah, do not make any debauchee a favour in my sight, for I have found in what You have revealed: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ up to His saying ﴿those, He has written faith in their hearts﴾."

That is, He created affirmation in their hearts, meaning those who do not ally with those who oppose Allah. It was also said: "kataba" means "athbata" (established), as said by al-Rabi' ibn Anas. It was also said: "jaʿala" (made), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So write us among the witnesses﴾, that is, make us; and His saying ﴿So I will write it for those who fear Allah﴾. It was also said: "kataba" means "jama'a" (gathered), and from it comes "al-katiba" (army), meaning they were not among those who say: "We believe in some and disbelieve in others."

The reading of the common people is with a fatha on the kaf of "kataba" and a fatha on the nun of "al-iman", meaning Allah wrote, and this is the better reading, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾. Abu al-Aliya, Zirr ibn Hubaysh and al-Mufaddal from Asim read "kutiba" in the passive, with "al-iman" in the nominative. Zirr ibn Hubaysh read "wa-ʿashiratihim" with an alif and a kasra on the ta', in the plural, and al-A'mash narrated it from Abu Bakr from Asim. It was also said: "kataba fi qulubihim" means "ʿala qulubihim" (upon their hearts), as in His saying concerning "fi judhu' al-nakhl" (on the trunks of the palm trees). The heart was singled out for mention because it is the place of faith. ﴿And strengthened them﴾: He empowered them and gave them victory ﴿with a spirit from Him﴾. Al-Hasan said: and with help from Him. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: with the Qur'an and its proofs. Ibn Juraij said: with light, faith, proof and guidance. It was also said: with a mercy from Allah. Some of them said: He strengthened them with Jibril, peace be upon him. ﴿And He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him﴾, that is, He accepted their deeds and they were pleased with Him, rejoicing in what He had given them. ﴿Those are the party of Allah. Indeed, the party of Allah are the successful﴾. Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Jurjani said, from some of his shaykhs: Dawud, peace be upon him, said: "My God! Who is Your party, and who surrounds Your Throne?" So Allah revealed to him:

"O Dawud, those whose eyes lower their gaze, whose hearts are pure, whose hands are clean; those are My party and those who surround My Throne."

Finished, and praise be to Allah, the surah "al-Mujadila".
